summary: Implemented cross-LAN firewall using Ansible run from node4 (the cluster's Ansible controller). node1 (VyOS) routes between lan-a (eth1, 10.50.10.0/24, node2) and lan-b (eth2, 10.50.20.0/24, node3). VyOS forward-filter firewall: rule 10 accepts established/related, rule 20 accepts TCP/5432 from eth1→eth2 (node2→node3), rules 30/40 explicitly reject all other eth1↔eth2 traffic in both directions, default-action drop as backstop (VyOS's default-action leaf only supports drop/accept, not reject, so explicit reject rules cover the "reject all other traffic" requirement). Verified end-to-end: TCP/5432 node2→node3 succeeds; other ports, ICMP, and the reverse direction on 5432 are all rejected with ICMP port-unreachable. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol on all 4 nodes (node1 VyOS, node2, node3, node4) one at a time — captured boot_id baselines, restarted each via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified recovery (interfaces, routes, firewall rules, and actual TCP/ICMP behavior all intact after reboot). Discovered and fixed a persistence gap: node1's ad-hoc ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for the vyos user did not survive VyOS's reboot (not part of its config-store persistence), so re-added the cluster SSH key via VyOS's native `set system login user vyos authentication public-keys` config path, which does persist; re-ran the Ansible playbook afterward to confirm full idempotent success across all three managed hosts.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router (eth1/eth2 unconfigured), node2 on lan-a (ens7), node3 on lan-b (ens7), node4=Ansible controller with ansible-core 2.20.5
Distributed CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to node1 (vyos user filesystem authorized_keys, later superseded by persistent VyOS config), node2 and node3 (antrieb user)
Wrote Ansible inventory.ini and playbook.yml on node4 under /root/cross-lan-firewall
Diagnosed and worked around: ansible-core 2.20 module python requirements incompatible with node2/3's Python 3.5/2.7 (switched lan_nodes tasks to raw module, no facts gathering)

Diagnosed and fixed: global ansible.cfg become=True double-sudo wrapping broke VyOS bash alias expansion for 'configure'; disabled become on router play and called sudo -n explicitly inside the raw command

Diagnosed and fixed: chaining VyOS set commands with '&&' broke bash alias expansion timing (alias only usable once a full statement had been read); switched to newline-separated commands matching the vyos-reference pattern

Diagnosed and fixed: VyOS default-action only supports drop|accept (not reject) per node.def; implemented default-action drop plus explicit reject rules (30/40) for all other cross-LAN traffic in both directions to satisfy the 'reject' requirement

Applied final playbook: node1 gets eth1=10.50.10.254/24, eth2=10.50.20.254/24 and the forward-filter firewall policy; node2/node3 get static ens7 addressing plus cross-subnet routes via node1, persisted through /etc/network/interfaces.d
Verified TCP/5432 node2->node3 allowed and all other ports/ICMP/reverse-direction rejected using a socat listener and nc/ping tests

Ran mandatory restart protocol sequentially on node1, node2, node3, node4: captured boot_id baseline, triggered native reboot (systemctl reboot on VyOS/node4 as root, sudo -n reboot on node2/node3 as antrieb), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified service/config/data recovery

Found and fixed a persistence gap on node1: ad-hoc filesystem authorized_keys for vyos user did not survive reboot; re-added the cluster key via VyOS's native 'set system login user vyos authentication public-keys' config (which does persist) and committed/saved
Re-ran the full Ansible playbook after all four restarts to confirm idempotent 'already exists / nothing to commit' success across all three managed hosts
Performed a final end-to-end connectivity/rejection test after all restarts to confirm the firewall policy is fully intact
